pr_body:
Replaces #6485 

Move the payload handling logic to a discrete go module so we can start to lay the foundation to toggle between C++ and Go runner implementation at build time.

This change adjusts how to handle runner payloads to support container builds where we keep them extracted in the filesystem. This makes it easier to optimize the cpu/cuda vs cpu/rocm images for size, and should result in faster startup times for container images.

Looks like container startup time is down to ~100ms on a warm system.

ROCm image updated to use a base ubuntu image and just use our libraries. The official images and packages pull in compilers as dependencies so this seems to be the optimal lean setup.

Fixes #6541
pr_comments:

wow, impressive!

review_comments: This can be in a follow-up since it might affect the directory structure of the embed.FS, but do we need the subdirectories to all be checked in (vs a single `placeholder` file in `build/`?

I think the layout is required in order to handle the cross-compilation wrinkle.  In particular darwin, but theoretically building on native linux might apply too.  We don't want to ingest the payloads from the "other" architecture(s) into the binary for a given architecture, which requires being explicit in the glob to select only the current architecture.
Got it. I was wondering if we need the shell directories for all the archs (maybe the build/tests would fail?)
`embed_windows.go`? I guess that may break the build on other platforms
I'm not sure how other OSes are building given the way we have the generate scripts set up, but my thinking was to not attempt to ingest payloads on them and leave the runners external.
